1. Core Clinical Tension: A young schoolteacher presents with a painless, slowly progressive 2-year swelling of the flexor aspect of the index finger and palm ('sausage finger') without constitutional symptoms, history of exposure, or osseous lesions on plain radiograph. Initial cytology showing giant cells strongly supported a benign synovial neoplasm (giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath), masking an indolent tuberculous tenosynovitis characterized by rice bodies.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission evaluation ends after physical examination and initial plain radiography of the hand, prior to surgical exploration of the flexor tendon sheath.
3. Differential Distinctions: Giant cell tumor of the tendon sheath presents as a firm, lobulated, slow-growing soft tissue mass in the fingers, but histopathology shows multinucleated giant cells within a background of round/polygonal mononuclear cells without granulomas or rice bodies. Compound palmar ganglion and tendinous xanthoma produce localized flexor tendon swelling, but lack tuberculous caseating granulomas. Tuberculous tenosynovitis classically forms a thickened synovial sheath filled with fibrin-rich 'rice bodies' and chronic Langhans-type granulomatous inflammation.
case_prompt: A 30-year-old male teacher presents to the outpatient clinic with a 2-year history of slowly progressive swelling of the right index finger, accompanied by dull pain and difficulty flexing the digit. He reports no history of trauma, drug abuse, or systemic illnesses. On physical examination, there is a prominent swelling involving the flexor aspect of the right index finger extending onto the palm. A plain radiograph of the finger demonstrates normal bony structures, with the phalanges and the second metacarpal free from visible lesions.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Giant Cell Tumour (GCT) of the Tendon Sheath
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered the leading provisional diagnosis due to the chronic, painless, lobulated soft-tissue mass along the flexor tendon sheath; however, surgical exploration revealed a synovial sac distended by rice bodies and histopathology showed chronic granulomatous inflammation rather than a true neoplasm.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A provisional diagnosis of GCT of flexor tendon sheath and a differential diagnosis of compound palmar ganglion and tendinous xanthoma was kept, and the patient was planned for exploration/excision after taking consent for amputation of the digit.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Compound Palmar Ganglion and Tendinous Xanthoma
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Maintained on the differential diagnosis for chronic swelling of the flexor tendon sheath and palm; excluded when surgical exploration uncovered a thickened sheath packed with shiny rice bodies and confluent Langhans giant-cell granulomas.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: and a differential diagnosis of compound palmar ganglion and tendinous xanthoma was kept, and the patient was planned for exploration/excision after taking consent for amputation of the digit.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Surgical exposure revealed a synovial sheath distended with copious rice bodies, and histopathology confirmed confluent epithelioid granulomas with Langhans giant cells; subsequent sputum testing yielded acid-fast bacilli, confirming tuberculous tenosynovitis and leading to complete cure with anti-tuberculosis therapy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: sections from the cyst wall showed fibrocollagenous tissue diffusely infiltrated by confluent granulomas [Figures 6 and 7] comprising of epithelioid cells, lymphocytes, plasma cells and Langhan's type giant cells suggesting TB.
